subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider text like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron and model-fallback behavior?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the right permanent class affects retry matching, cross-provider fallback, and whether shared auth profiles are cooled down during provider 500 outages.

options.title: Classify as server_error without cooldown
options.body: Map the plain api-error internal-server shape into the existing `server_error` reason so cron retry/state and model fallback can act on it without poisoning shared auth-profile health.

options.title: Classify as overloaded with cooldown
options.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as provider overload so same-provider profiles are skipped faster, accepting broader shared cooldown impact during provider outages.

options.title: Keep timeout and add cron-local handling
options.body: Leave global failover classification unchanged and add a cron-local provider-outage retry/alert rule, which reduces auth-profile risk but adds another decision path.

recommendation.title: Classify as server_error without cooldown
recommendation.body: Map the plain api-error internal-server shape into the existing `server_error` reason so cron retry/state and model fallback can act on it without poisoning shared auth-profile health.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf carried the closest merged structured `server_error` retry work and follow-up classification fixes, so they have the best recent context for the remaining policy choice.
